Distributed Runner

At-least-once batch processing across instances, backed by an embedded redb store and (optionally) Raft-replicated coordination.

Overview

The distributed runner takes a Pipeline as a template and runs it against many partitions of data spread across instances. The mechanics are:

  1. An instance calls PartitionSource::claim_next_batch to lease a row-range partition.
  2. It reconstructs a Dataset for the partition (via a user-provided world_factory closure).
  3. It calls PipelineRuntime::run_on_with_state(&mut partition_dataset, prior) — the template’s own data, sources, and sinks are never used. prior is the opaque state blob the runtime returned for its previous batch; whatever it returns now is persisted and handed back next time.
  4. Between (configurable) stages, it persists Arrow IPC checkpoints via CheckpointStore::save_checkpoint.
  5. On success it acks the claim; on crash, the lease expires and another instance picks the partition up, optionally resuming from the latest checkpoint.

The runner is feature-gated. Plain distributed gives you the traits, redb-backed store, and runner. Adding distributed-raft wires the store’s state machine to openraft so coordination state is replicated across nodes.

Building blocks

TypeRole
PartitionSourceClaims, renews, acks, and releases row-range batches across instances. Lease-based to handle crashes.
CheckpointStorePersists Arrow IPC snapshots keyed by (claim_id, stage_idx) for crash recovery.
RedbSharedStoreImplements both traits over redb. Single-node mode applies state directly; cluster mode proposes through a Raft channel.
DistributedRunnerThe driver. Holds a pipeline template, a runtime, and a RunnerConfig. run(world_factory) loops until exhausted.
RunnerConfiginstance_id, checkpoint_strategy, schema_id, max_batches, lease renewal interval.
CheckpointStrategyHow often to checkpoint: EveryStage, EveryNStages(n), or None.

Single-node example

The simplest setup uses one process, one redb file, and a single instance running its own coordinator. There is no Raft: RedbSharedStore::single_node applies every command directly to the local database. Cluster mode keeps the pipeline template and the run call identical — only the store construction changes, and it gains a Raft driver. 

use std::path::Path;

use pcs_core::prelude::*;
use pcs_service::distributed::{
    CheckpointStrategy, DistributedRunner, RedbSharedStore, RunnerConfig,
};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> PcsResult<()> {
    // 1. Open the shared redb store. Single-node applies state straight to the
    //    local file — no Raft, no second database.
    let store = RedbSharedStore::single_node(Path::new("/var/lib/pcs/pcs.redb"))?;

    // 2. Register a master batch — the rows this runner partitions over.
    //    `ipc_bytes` is an Arrow IPC *stream* (`arrow_ipc::writer::StreamWriter`)
    //    of at most MAX_LOG_ENTRY_BYTES (1 MiB). Split larger inputs into
    //    several batches, each with its own `batch_id`.
    let (ipc_bytes, total_rows) = encode_trades_ipc("/data/trades.parquet")?;
    store
        .register_master_batch(
            0,                         // batch_id
            Trade::name().to_string(), // component
            1,                         // schema_id
            ipc_bytes,
            total_rows,                // u32 rows in this batch
        )
        .await?;

    // 3. Build the pipeline template. Its own dataset, sources, and sinks are
    //    never used — every claim runs against a fresh partition Dataset.
    let template = Pipeline::builder("trade-processor")
        .with::<Trade>()
        .with_system(ValidateTradeSystem)
        .with_system(EnrichTradeSystem)
        .build();

    // 4. Drive the runner. `run` takes `&self`; `world_factory` is called once
    //    per claim to produce the empty Dataset the partition is loaded into.
    let runner = DistributedRunner::new(
        store,
        Box::new(template),
        RunnerConfig {
            checkpoint_strategy: CheckpointStrategy::EveryStage,
            schema_id: 1,
            max_batches: None,
            ..Default::default()
        },
    );
    let processed = runner.run(Dataset::new).await?;
    println!("processed {processed} batches");
    Ok(())
}

Checkpoints & recovery

Checkpoints serialize the partition’s Dataset after a stage completes and persist the bytes via CheckpointStore. If the instance crashes mid-pipeline, the next claim of the same partition restores the latest checkpoint and resumes from the next stage.

Three policies trade durability against throughput:

  • EveryStage — safest; one fsync per stage.
  • EveryNStages(n) — tunable; pick n based on stage cost.
  • None — fastest; on crash, the entire partition replays from scratch.

Cluster mode (feature = "distributed-raft")

The distributed-raft feature replaces the single-node store with a Raft-coordinated one. Two redb files back the cluster:

  • Log file — written by ArrowRedbLogStore, openraft’s RaftLogStorage implementation.
  • State machine file — written by ArrowRedbStateMachine, applying ConsensusCommand ops.

A ConsensusCommand is the deterministic op type proposed via Raft — claim, renew, ack, release, register-batch, save-checkpoint. The leader serializes ops, replicates them to followers, and applies them to the redb state machine on commit. 

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use pcs_service::distributed::RedbSharedStore;
use pcs_service::distributed::consensus::{ArrowRaftDriver, ArrowRaftDriverConfig};

// `start` is async. It opens both redb files, refuses to start if the state
// machine is behind what the log store already purged, and returns the handle
// plus the driver's task — keep that task alive for the process lifetime.
let (handle, _driver_task) = ArrowRaftDriver::start(
    ArrowRaftDriverConfig {
        node_id: 1,
        listen_addr: "0.0.0.0:7001".parse().unwrap(),
        // "host:port" strings, resolved lazily at connect time, so Docker
        // service names work. An empty map auto-initialises a single node.
        peers: HashMap::from([
            (2, "pcs-2:7001".to_string()),
            (3, "pcs-3:7001".to_string()),
        ]),
        ..Default::default()
    },
    "/var/lib/pcs/raft-log.redb",      // openraft log store
    "/var/lib/pcs/state-machine.redb", // applied state
)
.await?;

// `start` wires outbound connections only. Until the inbound listener is
// spawned, peers cannot deliver votes or heartbeats and no leader is elected.
let _tcp_server = handle.spawn_tcp_server("0.0.0.0:7001".parse().unwrap());

// Multi-node store: mutations are proposed through Raft, reads lock the very
// same database handle the state machine writes to — no second open file.
let store = RedbSharedStore::multi_node(Arc::clone(handle.app_db()), handle.clone());
// ... same pipeline template, same `runner.run(Dataset::new)` call as single-node.

One node bootstraps the cluster once: handle.initialize(members) takes a BTreeMap<u64, openraft::BasicNode> of the initial membership and is a no-op on later starts. Skip it entirely when peers is empty — ArrowRaftDriver::start auto-initialises that case. The pcs-service binary run with mode = "cluster" performs all of the wiring above from TOML, so hand-rolling it is only necessary when embedding the runner in your own process.

Peer framing is length-prefixed TCP with a 16 MiB frame cap. The driver builds the outbound half (TcpNetworkFactory → TcpNetwork) internally and calling code never names either type, so adding nodes needs only reachable TCP ports plus the spawn_tcp_server listener above.
